 A violent vacation: The poker vlogger trading cash games for GTA VI
 Mike Patrick Posted on: November 17, 2026 08:19 PST Link copied Add as a preferred
source on Google 
 “I’ll be dead to the world and only accepting sliced lunch meats slid underneath my office door.”
 Words from a dedicated online poker grinder, strapping in for a marathon session or a high-volume Sunday grind?
 Nope, it’s a statement of what to expect from popular poker vlogger and player Jaman Burton come this Thursday, November 19: the day the entire world changes with the release of Grand Theft Auto V I .
 Don't expect to see Jaman Burton on the felt anytime soon after November 19. Austin Currington 
 The GTA phenomenon
 That may sound like an excessively bold statement for the release of a videogame, but GTA VI is more than that; it's an entertainment phenomenon. The series has grossed an estimated $13.6 billion since its original incarnation in 1997, and is one of the biggest entertainment IPs ever. 
 GTA VI alone has already made  over $1B in pre-orders before the game is even available to play.
 The release of this newest edition has created a years-long frenzy of anticipation — 13 years, in fact, since GTA V — with millions of fans worldwide clamouring for this latest release in their beloved series until it is finally launched on Thursday.
 We imagine the poker scene in Vice City is as hot as it is in real-life Florida. 
 People are  booking time off work , vacationing, and essentially stepping away from their real lives to dive into the world of Vice City and Leonida. It’s an immaculate and extreme recreation of Miami and Florida, which the series first introduced with what many consider the best game of the series, and Burton’s favorite, GTA : Vice City in 2002.
 Several poker players have told us that they’ll be taking some time away from the felt when the game is released at midnight on Thursday , and they have a well-known and respected ally in the creative vlogger and gamer, Burton.
 As an all-time fan of the series, Burton is as hyped for GTA VI as anyone. He’ll be one of those 'vacationing' from his regular life, trading in vlogging and cash games in the city GTA: San Andreas recreated in 2004 as Las Venturas , for a life of virtual crime in the neon-lit streets of Vice City.
 We spoke to him about why GTA VI is worth locking himself away, how long he’ll be in his office living off of door-slid sandwich meats (okay, we’re pretty sure he’s actually going to eat – and might even sleep), and what the hype of GTA VI would be remotely on par with in the poker world.
 Long before poker and GTA, the Atari 2600 was a young Burton's game of choice. Hayley Hochstetler 
 SPECIAL OFFERS 
 Leaving the poker room for Vice City
 “I’ve been playing GTA since the original," says Burton. "Yes: the top-down version. It came out when I was in college, and my roommates and I skipped a lot of classes because we were so enthralled by it.
 "I have stories and memories tied to every GTA release since. I remember living in Springfield, Illinois, and playing Vice City with friends all night long.”
 Almost 30 years ago, the original GTA gave birth to an empire that will be tearing poker players away from the tables this week. 
 Burton has been a gamer his whole life, dating back to the earliest days of the technology, when the disappointing 1980s Atari 2600 releases of  Pac-Man and the ill-fated E.T. The Extra-Terrestrial game were the peak of videogame hype.
 But now, at the age where he qualifies for 50+ seniors' poker tournaments and with responsibilities, a daughter, and a poker-playing partner in Lily Newhouse , life isn’t as simple as skipping classes to immerse himself in the world of GTA .
 “Lily isn’t a fan of the game’s mature themes. She thinks the whole thing is silly, but she tries to understand. I let her know this was coming about a year ago. My daughter is a gamer herself, so she understands, although this isn’t really her genre. She’s more into The Sims and The Legend of Zelda .”
 While also an all-time gaming great, The Legend of Zelda this ain't. 
 But what about the vlog? And playing poker?
 Burton’s responsibilities include his award-winning poker vlog, The Drawing Dead ,  which fans can be assured won’t be going on hiatus. Burton is preparing episodes for release right through the end of 2026, allowing him to be away from the Bellagio felt for the Vice City beaches.
 But what of missed opportunities in the poker room? A successful player on the felt, Burton says he’ll be just fine taking time away from that game, for this game.
 “Money doesn’t drive me anymore. The entire reason I made money was to have the freedom to do what I want, and this is a manifestation of that. I guess it could be considered a vacation, sure, but not just from poker. From everything . I plan on being completely disconnected.”
 Come Thursday, you'll be seeing Burton taking down banks in GTA VI instead of taking down pots. 
 Still, isn’t this a bit extreme?
 Disconnecting from everything. Preparing weeks of content in advance. Avoiding the poker world for what he says will be at least three weeks.
 When has any form of entertainment had the capability of taking over a person’s life in such a manner?
 Burton is not some extreme example within our little microcosm of the universe that we know as the poker world; GTA VI is an entity that has prompted companies and even governments to send out memos and social media messages about the right way to ask for time off around November 19.
 Important questions are being asked online. 
 Some lesser-populated poker rooms and players committing to their win rate flatlining for a few weeks is just something we in our world will be dealing with, and Burton summed up why.
 “I honestly think  this will be the biggest cultural event of the year . Even if the game is horrible and a flop, it’ll be bigger than anything else that happens in 2026... including Texas going 'blue.' As far as a poker comparison, I’d compare it to, well... nothing. Maybe if Ivey, Daniel, and Hellmuth were three-handed for the Main Event bracelet , the poker world might approach this level of anticipation.”
 Editor's Note: Our thoughts go out to this article's author Mike Patrick, who has reported the early signs of illness and may need a few days off to recover (starting Thursday, at midnight). Get well soon.
